lines.text: Hi, I'm Sindy! Let's fix a cluster that won't come up.
You create a cluster with many nodes, and it fails. Some containers start fine, others crash within the first second.
It typically happens at eight nodes or more. Let's find out why, and fix it.
The error names the node that never got ready, and exit code two fifty-five.
It reads one way if the container had already exited when sind checked, and another if it died while sind was waiting.
Exit code two fifty-five means that systemd, PID 1 inside the container, failed during early start-up.
The most common cause is a Linux limit that's too low: the number of inotify instances per user.
Every container uses several, for the cgroup events that containerd watches, and systemd inside needs them too.
Once the limit is used up, new containers can't start systemd, and exit at once.
Many distributions default to a hundred and twenty-eight, enough for roughly ten to thirteen systemd containers.
To check, read the current limit. Here, it's a hundred and twenty-eight.
Then search the Docker logs for inotify errors. Too many open files means the limit ran out.
The fix: raise the limit. A value of ten twenty-four supports about a hundred containers.
The first command sets it right away, until the next reboot.
To keep it, write the setting to a file, and reload all settings.
Docker needs no restart: new containers get the new limit immediately.
So: exit code two fifty-five points to the inotify limit. Check it, raise it, and make the new value stick.
sind doctor checks this limit for you: next up, Diagnostics. See you there!
